question: List all customer names and emails.
Show all products with a price greater than 50.
How many orders are there in total?
expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_orders FROM orders;

question: List all products in the 'Electronics' category sorted by price descending.
expected_sql: SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE category = 'Electronics' ORDER BY price DESC;

question: Find the top 5 most expensive products.
expected_sql: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 5;

question: Show total revenue per product category.
expected_sql: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;

question: Find the average order value per customer.
expected_sql: SELECT c.name, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_value FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY avg_order_value DESC;

question: Which customers have placed more than 3 orders?
expected_sql: SELECT c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name HAVING COUNT(o.id) > 3 ORDER BY order_count DESC;

question: Show the average review rating per product, only for products with at least 5 reviews.
expected_sql: SELECT p.name, AVG(r.rating) AS avg_rating, COUNT(r.id) AS review_count FROM products p JOIN reviews r ON p.id = r.product_id GROUP BY p.id, p.name HAVING COUNT(r.id) >= 5 ORDER BY avg_rating DESC;

question: Show monthly revenue for the last 12 months.
expected_sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date) AS month, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.id = oi.order_id WHERE o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '12 months' GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date) ORDER BY month;

question: Rank customers by their total spending using a window function.
expected_sql: SELECT c.name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(o.total_amount) DESC) AS spending_rank FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name;

question: Calculate the running total of daily revenue.
expected_sql: SELECT order_date, daily_revenue, SUM(daily_revenue) OVER (ORDER BY order_date) AS running_total FROM (SELECT DATE(order_date) AS order_date, SUM(total_amount) AS daily_revenue FROM orders GROUP BY DATE(order_date)) daily ORDER BY order_date;

question: Find products that have never been ordered.
expected_sql: SELECT p.name, p.price FROM products p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi WHERE oi.product_id = p.id);

question: Using a CTE, find the top 3 customers by revenue and show their most recent order date.
expected_sql: WITH customer_revenue AS (SELECT c.id, c.name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue, MAX(o.order_date) AS last_order_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name) SELECT name, total_revenue, last_order_date FROM customer_revenue ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 3;

question: Calculate each product's revenue share as a percentage of total revenue, and show the cumulative percentage.
expected_sql: WITH product_revenue AS (SELECT p.name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.id, p.name) SELECT name, revenue, ROUND(100.0 * revenue / SUM(revenue) OVER (), 2) AS pct_of_total, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY revenue DESC) / SUM(revenue) OVER (), 2) AS cumulative_pct FROM product_revenue ORDER BY revenue DESC;

question: Find customers whose average order value is above the overall average order value.
expected_sql: WITH overall_avg AS (SELECT AVG(total_amount) AS avg_val FROM orders) SELECT c.name, AVG(o.total_amount) AS customer_avg FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name HAVING AVG(o.total_amount) > (SELECT avg_val FROM overall_avg) ORDER BY customer_avg DESC;
